correctness.rationale: For a finite d-point sample, each selected circular coordinate induces a cyclic ordering; a connected arc has exactly consecutive-subset traces, and ties cannot enlarge them. Conversely independent strict cyclic orders can be embedded as d distinct vectors in (S1)^l. One order contributes d distinct k-subsets for 1<=k<d, giving l*d>=C(d,floor(d/2)). Explicit families for d=3,4,5,6,7 use 1,2,2,4,5 cyclic orders and independently cover every subset. The middle-layer inequalities exclude d=4 for l=1, d=6 for l<=3, d=7 for l<=4, d=8 for l<=8. Therefore the eight exact VC dimensions (3,5,5,6,7,7,7,7) follow; all endpoint and constant-label cases are included.

evidence: K_7^(3) tight Hamilton-cycle decompositions cover 3-subsets but do not automatically certify all lower-size subsets and the circular-coordinate learning class.
The general middle-layer obstruction is established here for every d and is sharp at d=3..7 by explicit cycles.

value.rationale: The smallest circular-feature budgets needed to shatter d=3..7 points are a natural statistical learning capacity invariant. Exact small-d obstructions and explicit witnesses distinguish circular stumps from ordinary linear stumps and resolve the first eight feature budgets; this is more than a renaming of the known 7-triple design.

limitations: Connected arcs on precisely one selected coordinate; no intersections/unions or arbitrary feature counts beyond eight.
